---
title: "Compute a Spinorama from your measurements"
date: 2026-08-22
abstract: >
  Generate Spinorama graphs and preference scores from a local measurement set
  without adding it to the full database.
---

[`scripts/compute_spin.py`](../scripts/compute_spin.py) loads one speaker's
measurement directory, computes available Spinorama curves and preference
scores, and writes PNG and JSON output. It does not modify the metadata
database.

## Quick start

From the repository root, with the project environment available:

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py /path/to/measurement-data
```

The script tries to detect the format and speaker name from the directory. Use
`--verbose` or `-v` for additional logging:

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py /path/to/measurement-data --verbose
```

## Supported formats

| Format | Typical input | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `klippel` | `SPL Horizontal.txt`, `SPL Vertical.txt` | Klippel NFS text export |
| `princeton` | `*_H_IR.mat`, `*_V_IR.mat` | Princeton 3D3A impulse responses |
| `spl_hv_txt` | `*_H.txt`, `*_V.txt` | Generic angle text files |
| `gll_hv_txt` | One or more `.zip` files | GLL-extracted meridian/parallel data |
| `rew_text_dump` | `On Axis.txt`, `LW.txt`, `ER.txt`, `SP.txt` | REW text export |
| `webplotdigitizer` | `.json` or `.tar` | WebPlotDigitizer project |

The input files may be directly in the supplied directory or in a version
subdirectory. For ambiguous directories, force the format with `--format`.

## Options

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py DIRECTORY [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--format FORMAT` | `auto`, `klippel`, `princeton`, `spl_hv_txt`, `gll_hv_txt`, `rew_text_dump`, or `webplotdigitizer` |
| `--output-dir DIR` | Output directory; defaults to the input directory |
| `--speaker-name NAME` | Name used in output filenames; defaults to the directory name |
| `--width N` | Graph width in pixels; default `800` |
| `--height N` | Graph height in pixels; default `600` |
| `--symmetry MODE` | `auto`, `mirror`, `shift`, or `none`; default `auto` |
| `--force` | Overwrite existing output files |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | Enable verbose output |
| `--version` | Print the tool version |

For horizontal measurements, `mirror` copies positive angles to negative
angles and `shift` wraps measurements from 180–350 degrees to -180–0 degrees.
Use `none` when the files already contain the desired angle convention.

## Examples

Auto-detect the format and write output beside the input:

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py ./my_speaker_data
```

Force Klippel input and write to a separate directory:

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py ./my_speaker_data \
  --format klippel --output-dir ./graphs
```

Generate larger graphs and replace existing output:

```{.shell}
python scripts/compute_spin.py ./my_speaker_data \
  --width 1200 --height 900 --force
```

## Output

The output directory can contain:

- `{speaker}_CEA2034.png` and normalized CEA2034 graphs;
- on-axis, predicted in-room response, group-delay, and reflection graphs;
- horizontal and vertical SPL, contour, normalized contour, 3D contour, and
  radar graphs when the input format provides enough angular data; and
- `{speaker}_scores.json`, containing the computed preference-score fields.

The score summary printed by the script includes the preference score with and
without subwoofer, NBD terms, PIR smoothness, low-frequency extension, and
other available components. Missing or incomplete measurements may cause some
graphs or score fields to be omitted.

To add the result to the shared database after inspecting it, place the source
files in the normal measurement tree and use the [metadata manager](03_metadata.qmd)
to record the speaker and measurement metadata.
